why: the goal callback's accept/reject/defer decision. rclcpp_action's `GoalResponse` has the same three cases; rclc's action server returns a bare `bool`. Ours is an enum because ACCEPT_AND_DEFER and ACCEPT_AND_EXECUTE are different arena transitions. NOTE the discriminants do not match rclcpp_action's: ours are 0-based (0/1/2), rclcpp_action's are 1-based (1/2/3), and the enumerators are `Reject` vs `REJECT`. The correlator sees only the NAME, so this pair reports as `same`; enumerator comparison is a feature it does not have, which is why the fact lives here. DECIDED (issue 0796) NOT to align, for two reasons. (1) These are not preferences but a C ABI: the value crosses three FFI seams as an integer -- a `#[repr(i8)]` Rust enum returned directly from `extern "C"` trampolines, `rclc_goal_response_t` / `rclc_cancel_response_t`, and an `enum class : int32_t` in C++ -- so renumbering is the kind of break that produces NO compile error anywhere, just a half-rebuilt tree that starts deciding accept where it meant reject. (2) It would buy nothing anyway: a ported `switch` still names `rclcpp_action::GoalResponse::REJECT`, so it must be edited regardless, and once edited it uses OUR enumerators and gets the right value under either numbering. Only code that hardcodes the integers is affected, and that code is already wrong. Against that, `Reject` = 0 is load-bearing: the arena's decision slots are zero-initialised static storage with no allocator and no constructor, and the null-callback path yields `Default`, so 0 MUST mean reject. Making 0 invalid would make "nobody answered" mean accept.
